## Report: `chaos-shop-base/api-memory-limit-restore-128mi-prod` released to prod

All three prod clusters are recovered: the api runs with a 128Mi limit, api and web are 2 of 2 available, no api pod has restarted since the rollout, and ConfigHub reports each Space Synced and Healthy. Nothing was refused and nothing failed to recover.

| Space | Release published (UTC) | New pods started | 2 of 2 available | ConfigHub Healthy | 3 min without restart confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| chaos-shop-prod-eu | 17:58:46 | 17:59:49, 17:59:51 | 17:59:57 | 18:01:39 | 18:02:53 |
| chaos-shop-prod-us-1 | 18:02:57 | 18:03:53, 18:04:01 | 18:04:05 | 18:05:28 | 18:07:05 |
| chaos-shop-prod-us-2 | 18:07:09 | 18:08:02, 18:08:08 | 18:08:12 | 18:09:37 | 18:11:14 |

- **Recovery per cluster:** service was back about 70 seconds after each publish, as soon as the new pods were Ready; web recovered by itself once the api answered.
- **Why three minutes is enough:** at the 40Mi limit the old pods were OOMKilled about 36 seconds after each start. The new pods have run well past that with zero restarts — 11 minutes on prod-eu, 7 on prod-us-1, 3 on prod-us-2 at the last reading.
- **Transient failure on every cluster:** Sveltos recorded "api: 1 of 2 updated" from a reading taken mid-rollout, so ConfigHub showed Degraded/Failed for about 80 seconds. It cleared on Sveltos's next retry each time, without any action.
- **Fleet check:** the `chaos-shop` ClusterHealthCheck passes on staging, prod-eu, prod-us-1 and prod-us-2 (read at 18:09:45).

I could not read actual memory use, because `kubectl top` was not permitted, so "the cache has filled" rests on the pods surviving well beyond the old kill point rather than on a measured figure.
